60f1d313dd6a.question: What did you do last weekend?
60f1d313dd6a.text: Last weekend was pretty quiet, to be honest. On Saturday morning I had a lie in, which I don't usually get because of my shifts, and then I went down to the shops to get food for the week. In the afternoon I watched the football at the pub with a couple of lads from work. We lost two nil, which was annoying, but it was still a good afternoon out. I got home about six and made a chicken curry, the one I always make, and watched a bit of telly before bed. Sunday I went round to my mum's for lunch. My sister was there as well with her little boy, so it was nice to see them. Mum did a roast like she always does. I came back in the evening, sorted my washing and got my uniform ready for Monday. Nothing exciting really, but it was a decent weekend and I felt rested by the end of it.

72f6bda4ae90.persona: 34-year-old man, lives alone, part-time warehouse shifts, likes football and cooking
72f6bda4ae90.question: Can you tell me a bit about your job?
72f6bda4ae90.text: I work part time at a warehouse on the industrial estate, it's for an online retailer, so mostly clothes and homeware. I do about twenty five hours a week, usually four shifts. My job is picking, so I get a handheld scanner that tells me what items to collect and which aisle they're in, and I fill a trolley and take it to the packing area. It's quite physical, you walk miles in a shift, my phone said fifteen kilometres one day. The targets can be stressful, they track how many items you pick per hour, and if you fall behind your supervisor has a word. But the people are alright, there's a good bunch on my shift and we have a laugh at break. I've been there about three years now. It's not what I want to do forever, but it pays the rent and the hours work for me at the moment. I'd like to move into the stock control side eventually.

278bc3822f2a.text: My family's quite small really. There's my mum, who lives about twenty minutes away on the bus, and my younger sister, who's thirty and has a little boy who's just turned two. a531ab04c0c7.persona: 34-year-old man, lives alone, part-time warehouse shifts, likes football and cooking
a531ab04c0c7.question: What was it like where you grew up?
a531ab04c0c7.text: I grew up in a small seaside town on the east coast, about two hours from here. It was the kind of place that was busy in summer with tourists and dead quiet the rest of the year. We lived in a terraced house about ten minutes' walk from the beach. As kids we spent most of our time outside, riding bikes along the seafront, playing football on the green, or hanging around the arcades when we had a bit of money. There wasn't much work there, which is why a lot of people moved away when they finished school, including me. My dad worked at the docks until they closed, and that hit the town hard. Looking back, it was a safe place to grow up and I had good mates, but it felt a bit stuck. I still go back sometimes, and it's changed a lot. Some of the old shops have gone, but the beach is the same.

dc3d05979316.question: What do you like to cook?
dc3d05979316.text: I really like cooking, it's probably my favourite way to relax after work. I mostly cook curries, because my mate at the warehouse taught me how to do a proper one from scratch, toasting the spices first, then onions, garlic, ginger, and letting it cook slowly. My chicken curry is the one I'm proudest of. I also do a decent spaghetti bolognese, and on Sundays when I'm not at my mum's I'll roast a chicken. I try to cook in big batches and freeze portions for the week, because after a long shift I don't want to start from nothing. Lately I've been trying to cook more vegetables, so I've been doing stir fries and a lentil soup that's surprisingly good. I watch cooking shows for ideas, and sometimes I try something new on a day off. Not everything works, I burned a risotto last month, but I enjoy it, and it saves money compared to takeaways.

6899df75d7ad.question: Can you tell me a bit about your job?
6899df75d7ad.text: Yeah, sure. So I work part-time at a warehouse, just on the outskirts of town. Most of the shifts are evening or nights, so it can get a bit tiring but it suits me, since I’m not much of a morning person anyway. It’s mostly just stacking shelves, moving boxes around and keeping track of the stock. Sometimes we unload deliveries, which can be a bit heavy, but I’m used to it now. There’s a small team of us, and we all get along pretty well, usually. The work itself is quite straightforward and not too stressful. I’d say the only downside is the hours can be quite random, so you have to be a bit flexible with your time, but that means I get my days free sometimes. It’s not my dream job, but it pays the bills and gives me some time to focus on other things I enjoy, like watching football or trying new recipes.

bafde24bc905.question: What was it like where you grew up?
bafde24bc905.text: I grew up in a small town not far from here actually, so it wasn’t much of a change moving. It was quiet, pretty peaceful really. I remember it always felt a bit boring as a teenager, because there wasn’t loads to do, but looking back it was alright, really. I’m glad I grew up somewhere like that.
